clue.text: Used item H&M originally embossed with blue

indicators.note: what something is originally is how it begins, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the ampersand is read out as the word 'and' between the two letters

explanation.surface: A secondhand garment from the H&M chain, originally decorated with a blue embossed pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: H&M is the clothing chain, but here the ampersand is spelt out in full so the letters run H, AND, M.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-me-down is a garment or object passed on after an earlier owner has finished with it.

clue.text: Title of Austrian race announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word for race is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to hare is to race along at speed

explanation.surface: A question about the honorific belonging to some Austrian racing event.
explanation.walkthrough: Race is a verb here: to hare off is to run fast, and the German honorific is pronounced much like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is the German-language form of address equivalent to Mister, used in Austria.

clue.text: Young channel acquiring hot reporter

indicators.note: acquiring means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the channel word

blocks.note: a sound is a narrow sea channel
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A youth TV channel takes on a sensational journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel suggests television, but it is a strait of water, a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A newshound is an informal term for a keen journalist who chases stories.

clue.text: Upset some toddler on a mucky seat

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top
some of the following words means only a part of their run of letters is used

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of toddler, all of on and a, and the start of mucky

explanation.surface: A small child gets distressed sitting on a dirty chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat in the sense of a country seat is a landed estate, the home of the local lord.

clue.text: Government vehicle crushed by Mark's vehicle

indicators.note: something crushed by another is squeezed in between its parts, so it is placed inside

blocks.note: G is a standard abbreviation for government, and a car is a vehicle
a dot is a small mark

explanation.surface: An official car gets flattened by a vehicle belonging to someone called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name; it is a dot, and the 's simply means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogcart is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, originally with a box for carrying dogs.

clue.text: Birds flew at last over eastern States

indicators.note: at last points to the very end of the word, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: Birds finally migrate across the eastern United States.
explanation.walkthrough: States looks like the USA but is a verb meaning declares. In a down clue, over places one piece on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Weavers are small finch-like birds that knit elaborate nests out of grass.

clue.text: Suspect Yard follows in Fife at intervals

indicators.note: at intervals means taking letters spaced out, skipping one each time

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of in Fife
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A detective from Scotland Yard pursues a suspect in Fife, a county of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Yard and Suspect suggest Scotland Yard, but Yard is just the unit abbreviation, placed after the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iffy is informally dubious or questionable, much as a suspect thing is.

clue.text: Dress changing hands for lots of 5

indicators.note: hands are right and left, so changing hands swaps one of those letters for the other

explanation.surface: A dress passes from one owner to another.
explanation.walkthrough: The R (right) in the dress word swaps to L (left). The definition refers to 5 down's answer, birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock is a large gathering of birds, and the birds meant are those at 5 down.

clue.text: Beatles number maybe overly extended in the past

indicators.note: stretching a short span of time into a much longer one replaces the closing time unit

blocks.note: a famous Beatles song, one possible example of their numbers

explanation.surface: A Beatles song stretched out too long, in nostalgic mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The song title ends in DAY; extending that day to a YEAR gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear is a literary word for time gone by, the bygone era.

clue.text: Grain brewed in mist as woodland activity

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order
in places the mixed letters inside the word for mist

explanation.surface: Cereal fermented in a haze, as in some woodland brewing scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Foraging is searching for wild food such as mushrooms and berries, often in woods.

clue.text: Gold reflected by pale ash

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Gold mirrored against a pale ash-coloured background.
explanation.walkthrough: Ash looks like a pale grey colour that fits the surface, but it is a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan is also called the mountain ash, a tree with red berries.

clue.text: Alluring General on vacation up for some action?

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, so only the outside letters of the word remain

blocks.note: first and last letters of General

explanation.surface: An attractive army general on holiday is up for some military action.
explanation.walkthrough: Action in the surface means combat; the question mark flags the romantic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamorous means attractive in a dazzling way, which is what alluring describes.

clue.text: Deficiency in gear host fixed

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or rearranged, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A host repairs a fault in some equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage is a lack of something needed, which is what a deficiency means.

clue.text: Body part causes irritation when undressed

indicators.note: undressing strips off the outer layer, so the outside letters are removed

explanation.surface: A part of the body chafes when someone strips off.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between the foot and the leg, one part of the body.

clue.text: Seabirds the Greek ultimately raised in streams

indicators.note: in a down clue the final letter is lifted up to the top, moving end to start
in places the shifted name inside the word for streams

blocks.note: Zorba the Greek, the novel and film

explanation.surface: A Greek man finally brought up among some streams of seabirds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Greek' completes the title Zorba the Greek; its last letter is moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Razorbills are black and white auks with deep, blade-like beaks, nesting on sea cliffs.

clue.text: Five in pool session replacing fellow's drink

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another within the word

blocks.note: V is five in Roman numerals
aquafit is an exercise class held in a swimming pool
F is an abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Five people at a swimming class replace a man's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Aquafit, a water-exercise class, has its F swapped for the Roman five.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquavit is a Scandinavian spirit flavoured with caraway, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Infectious game advanced with six in the lead

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A contagious match moves on with six players ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Advanced means lent, as a loan is advanced; in the lead puts six first.
explanation.definitionFit: Virulent describes a disease that is highly harmful and spreads readily.

clue.text: Beer knocked back by far ramp in dock

indicators.note: knocked back pushes the word back the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: as in way off, far off

explanation.surface: A beer downed by someone far away at a quay.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocked back suggests drinking the beer, but it reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipway is a sloping ramp down into water where boats are built or launched.

clue.text: Screen background of jazz pianist entertaining Pulp

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them within your house, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Fats Waller, the American jazz pianist

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist plays host to the Britpop band Pulp in front of a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Pulp looks like the band but is soft mush. Fats Waller was a stride pianist of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallpaper on a computer is the image shown behind icons on the desktop screen.

clue.text: Told to do something neat

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to tidy up; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past participle of command and an adjective for tidily arranged.

clue.text: Thomas was this time put in taxi after party

indicators.note: to put something in is to place it inside, so one piece sits within the other
after means coming later, so the cab piece is placed second, behind the party word

explanation.surface: Thomas spent this time in a cab after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection until he saw it.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas questioned Christ's rising, hence the phrase doubting Thomas, a sceptic.

clue.text: Left city on river without right cook

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the river

blocks.note: the Niger, a West African river

explanation.surface: A cook moves out of a riverside city.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, on means placed after, so left and city follow the shortened river.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella Lawson is a famous British television cook, so the first name stands for a cook.

clue.text: Starting to develop article about fragrance

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the article runs back to front

explanation.surface: A newly launched article written about a perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being and beginning to grow.

clue.text: Leaf picked regularly from oldest herbs around

indicators.note: picking regularly takes every other letter, at even steps
around means turned round, so the picked letters run backwards

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A leaf gathered from the most ancient herbs nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Betel is the leaf of a climbing pepper plant, chewed with areca nut in Asia.

clue.text: Slow yankee replacing final third of blue box

indicators.note: the last third of the following word is taken out and the new letter put in its place

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the TARDIS, the blue police box time machine in Doctor Who

explanation.surface: A sluggish American swaps out part of a blue container.
explanation.walkthrough: The final third of the six-letter time machine is its last two letters, IS, which Y replaces. Doctor Who is a long-running British TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardy means late or sluggish in arriving, close to slow.

clue.text: Releases Scottish isle's urban music?

blocks.note: Unst, the most northerly of the Shetland Islands
raps are pieces of rap, a genre of urban music

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of city music a remote Scottish island has, the joke being Unst is anything but urban.
explanation.definitionFit: Unstraps means undoes the straps holding something, so it frees or releases it.

clue.text: Make changes to steps at back of class

blocks.note: RE is religious education, a school class
a jig is a lively dance with quick steps

explanation.surface: Changing the dance steps performed at the back of a class.
explanation.walkthrough: At back of puts the dance after the class, and RE is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejig is to rearrange or alter something, an informal word for making changes.

clue.text: London players raised zero capital

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upward, so the letters read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A London orchestra or team scrapes together no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Players and capital suggest sport and money; they are musicians and a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Large gent tore off glasses

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: L for large, as on clothing labels
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A big man rips off his spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held up to the eyes on a long handle.

clue.text: Tricks 60% of country with empty euphemisms

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word is its first three letters
an empty word has its insides removed, so only its outer letters remain

blocks.note: first and last letters of euphemisms

explanation.surface: Pranks performed by much of a nation using hollow, evasive language.
explanation.walkthrough: The country is Japan, of which three of five letters make sixty per cent.
explanation.definitionFit: Japes are jokes or pranks, playful tricks.

clue.text: Runner jams broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the airwaves, so the word is judged by its sound

explanation.surface: An athlete's signal blocks a radio transmission.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner is the crossword word for a river; this one is the river of the Greek underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The Styx is the mythical river souls cross into Hades, and rivers run.

clue.text: Just altered wonderful clothes worn by old star

indicators.note: only slightly changed, so the word's letters are rearranged a little

explanation.surface: Splendid costumes freshly tailored for a film star of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Just altered means only a small switch: two letters of the word for wonderful swap places.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood screen star of the 1920s and 1930s.
